newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares climb, lifted by dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares climb, lifted by dollar.

text.p: German shares crawled higher in early bourse trade on Thursday still unnerved by Wall Street's sharp drop a day earlier but supported by a slightly firmer dollar.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index was trading 7.73 points higher at 2,848.78 having come off its pre-bourse high at 2,856.44.

Dealers said the firmer dollar, trading at 1.5425 marks, was largely responsible for boosting the market this morning after it closely mirrored Wall Street's movements, falling in after-hours trading on Wednesday but recovering this morning.
The firmer dollar is particularly helpful for export sensitive shares, including chemicals.

Among the chemicals sector, Hoechst AG, fresh from announcing it would sell its specialty chemicals business to Swiss group Clariant AG and would buy the remaining stake in French drugs group Roussel-Uclaf, is still generating interest.
Separately electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG was down after a slew of mixed news, which some dealers thought was positive, although others disagreed.

Shipmaker Bremer Vulkan, once Germany's biggest shipyard, was the session biggest loser, as the bankrupt company said on Wednesday it had only enough money to keep its flagship yard open through the end of this year.
